selectionReason: RC63 stopped because the 2022 compact ladder lacked names and omitted the later SMC branch. The primary 2024 SMC study separately releases 88 named Cepheids, their three-filter observations, periods, geometry terms, and derived Wesenheit magnitudes. This makes a real named influence, calibration-transfer, and look-elsewhere audit possible without pretending that the unreleased current global covariance is available.
newVerifiedFacts: The official pinned tables contain 264 frame-level measurements and 88 Cepheid-level rows; every Cepheid has F555W, F814W, and F160W coverage.
Recomputing the published Wesenheit quantity from the rounded table columns leaves at most 0.001514 mag residual, consistent with tabular rounding.
After excluding the declared outlier OGLE-1455 and fixing the slope at -3.26, the reproduced intercept is 16.466751 mag and RMS scatter is 0.101624 mag, matching the paper's 16.467 and 0.1017.
The free-slope fit gives -3.315734+-0.052630, consistent with the published -3.31+-0.05.
OGLE-0896 has the largest leave-one-Cepheid-out pivot-zero-point displacement, only -0.002676 mag, equivalent to a linearized -0.123 percent distance-ladder scale change.
No geometry correction has 0.112333 mag RMS, the external eclipsing-binary plane has 0.102207 mag, and the published same-Cepheid plane has 0.101687 mag in sample.

A newly fitted same-Cepheid affine plane reaches 0.101759 mag training RMS but 0.105127 mag leave-one-out RMS, 0.002920 mag worse than the external eclipsing-binary plane; its tiny training gain does not transfer.

The frozen period-break scan peaks at logP=0.959 with statistic 1.944365. Repeating the entire scan in 20,000 null simulations gives global p=0.499725+-0.003535, so the selected break is not evidence of nonlinearity.
A dependency-free Node implementation reproduces the Python baseline, object influence, geometry transfer, and breakpoint bootstrap to numerical precision.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: The public named SMC tables reproduce the published fixed- and free-slope Cepheid calibration.
One SMC Cepheid moves the zero point by at least 0.01 mag when omitted.
A geometry plane optimized on the Cepheid residuals improves held-one-Cepheid prediction by at least 0.005 mag relative to external eclipsing-binary geometry.
A scanned period breakpoint is globally significant at p<0.01 under the frozen search.
Deleting the SMC anchor from the current full ladder moves global H0 by less than one full-fit sigma.

causalChain: Input and assumptions: pinned 2024 SMC frame and Cepheid tables, declared Wesenheit coefficient, fixed-slope baseline, one published outlier rule, external eclipsing-binary geometry, and a frozen breakpoint search.
Bottleneck: small in-sample residual improvements can arise from reusing the 87 retained Cepheids for model choice, while the current full-ladder covariance and row ancestry are still absent.
Bridge: use a geometry estimated from independent eclipsing binaries or evaluate a Cepheid-fitted plane on a held-out Cepheid; repeat the complete period-break search under the null.
Independent adjudicands: object-level zero-point displacement, held-one-Cepheid RMS, maximum-search bootstrap p-value, and agreement of separate Python and Node implementations.

Resolution criterion: the named SMC sub-branch passes object influence and independent calibration-transfer gates, then a current semantic ladder release supports covariance-preserving SMC deletion and independent global refit.

workPackages.purpose: Turn the SMC sub-branch into a reproducible named calibration fixture.
workPackages.method: Pin raw tables by commit and SHA-256; preserve Cepheid IDs, frame IDs, filters, geometry, selection, and transformation metadata; reproduce every published summary before sensitivity analysis.
workPackages.deliverable: Versioned 88-object fixture with parser, identity checks, baseline fit, and independent implementation receipt.
workPackages.pass: All 88 objects and 264 filter rows are present, derived magnitudes agree within 0.002 mag, and published intercept, scatter, and free slope pass frozen tolerances.
workPackages.fail: A missing filter, unidentified object, hash change, or baseline mismatch stops downstream claims.
workPackages.next: On failure, repair source semantics or parser before altering the scientific model.

workPackages.purpose: Adjudicate whether geometry and period structure transfer beyond the data that selected them.
workPackages.method: Compare no correction, external eclipsing-binary geometry, the published Cepheid plane, and a freshly fitted affine plane; evaluate the last by leave-one-Cepheid-out prediction. Scan frozen period pivots and bootstrap the complete maximum search.
workPackages.deliverable: Geometry training-versus-holdout table, period-break maximum-statistic null distribution, and explicit rejection or retention decisions.
workPackages.pass: A Cepheid-fitted geometry gains at least 0.005 mag over external geometry in leave-one-out RMS, or a period break reaches global p<0.01.
workPackages.fail: Training-only improvement or global p>=0.01 keeps external geometry and one-slope calibration primary.
workPackages.next: Use failed alternatives only as sensitivity analyses and search for an independent geometry or larger predeclared sample.

workPackages.purpose: Measure the SMC anchor's actual contribution to the current global distance ladder.
workPackages.method: Acquire current HST-JWST-SMC y-L-C arrays with observation and parameter dictionaries and covariance-component ancestry; validate Table2 Cepheid identities; remove SMC rows and descended covariance; refit independently.
workPackages.deliverable: Full-versus-no-SMC H0, rank, covariance rebuild hash, and held common-host residual table.
workPackages.pass: Two implementations agree, the reduced model remains identified, absolute H0 movement stays below one full-fit sigma, and held residuals meet their frozen budget.
workPackages.fail: Missing ancestry, rank loss, implementation disagreement, a one-sigma movement, or held residual failure makes SMC calibration the active problem.
workPackages.next: Only after passing should the early-universe model grid closed in RC62 and RC63 be reopened.

uncertaintyBudget: Photometric rounding: the public table is rounded, leaving a maximum 0.001514 mag reconstruction residual; this is smaller than the 0.01 mag influence gate but retained in the receipt.
Finite sample: 87 retained Cepheids share camera and calibration ancestors; leave-one-object-out diagnoses single-object leverage but is not a complete cluster-covariance estimate.
Geometry: the external eclipsing-binary plane has its own distance and planar-structure uncertainty; the audit tests relative transfer, not the full absolute DEB systematic budget.
Selection: OGLE-1455 is a published 3.4-sigma exclusion. Retaining it shifts the pivot zero point by 0.003788 mag, so the outlier rule remains visible.
Extinction law: changing the Wesenheit coefficient on total colour is confounded with the intrinsic period-colour relation. Only a residualized sensitivity is admissible without a joint colour model.
Search multiplicity: local breakpoint statistics are invalid after scanning pivots; the complete scan is repeated in each of 20,000 null simulations, with Monte Carlo SE 0.003535.
Global transport: sub-branch magnitude changes are linearized scale equivalents, not a covariance-preserving H0 refit; current global lineage remains the dominant unresolved uncertainty.
failedOrRejectedAttempts: The published same-Cepheid geometry reduces training RMS by roughly five ten-thousandths of a magnitude relative to external geometry, but a freshly optimized plane worsens held-one-Cepheid RMS; it is not promoted to the primary correction.

The winning breakpoint has different short- and long-period slopes, but half of null simulations produce an equal or larger maximum somewhere in the frozen search; the local-looking feature is rejected as evidence for a break.

A naive change from Wesenheit coefficient 0.386 to 0.362 moves the zero point by 0.024594 mag, but it applies a dust coefficient to total colour and therefore mixes intrinsic period-colour structure with extinction; the number is preserved as an inadmissible diagnostic, not a cosmological shift.
The SMC-only sub-branch cannot be converted into a current covariance-preserving global H0 deletion because no current global row, parameter, and covariance ancestry release was found.
structuralConnection: CONN-EVIDENCE-037 links calibration transfer, finite-sample influence, and post-selection inference: a model chosen on the same stars must earn its claim on held objects or a search-adjusted null distribution.
claimBoundary: RC64 reproduces and audits the named 2024 SMC Cepheid sub-branch. It does not recalculate the current global SH0ES covariance, prove that SMC cannot shift H0 materially, establish a universal Cepheid law, or resolve the Hubble tension.
exactNextStart: Obtain or construct a current semantic HST-JWST-SMC ladder release. Map the 88 Table2 Cepheid IDs and their frame IDs to global observation rows and covariance ancestors before viewing the no-SMC H0 result. Use external eclipsing-binary geometry as the primary SMC correction and the same-Cepheid plane only as a sensitivity branch. Execute covariance-preserving SMC deletion in two implementations; keep the early-physics grid closed unless the reduced fit remains identified, moves H0 by less than one full-fit sigma, and passes held common-host residuals.
